purpose: Define prose as a human-readable explanation layer that may summarize canonical semantics but may not be the sole carrier of machine-significant identity, Topic, structure, authority, behavior, causality, constraint or reference facts.

operations.name: Validate prose boundary
errors: machine-significant fact exists only in prose

operations.name: Generate human summary from canonical data

semantics.machine_semantics_rule: Every machine-significant fact stated in prose must already be represented in structured canonical data.
semantics.summary_rule: Prose may be generated from structured semantics.
semantics.conflict_rule: If prose contradicts structured canonical semantics, structured canonical semantics remain machine authority and the contradiction is a documentation/conformance failure.
semantics.localization_rule: Localized human prose may vary without changing canonical semantic identity.
semantics.omission_rule: Structured semantics remain valid even if prose is intentionally minimal.

invariants.rule: Machine-significant semantics are explicit and deterministic.

hard_gates.condition: machine-significant fact exists only in prose
reader must parse natural language to reconstruct identity, Topic, structure or causality
prose contradiction silently overrides structured semantics
localized prose changes canonical semantic identity
prose ordering is treated as execution order

references.purpose: Human prose is not substitute evidence for structured semantic claims.
Human prose can be rendered from normalized structured semantics.
